subject: Runtime degradation during Brightlane POC — mitigation & action items
messages:
From: Nina Park <nina@brightlane.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightlane POC Team <poc-team@brightlane.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick heads-up — intermittent streaming timeouts in POC

Hi Marissa —

We're seeing intermittent timeouts from our integration tests when clients open long-lived streaming sessions (10–60s). Failures spike when concurrency hits ~40 streams; below that it looks fine. Attached a zipped trace set (trace-20270410.zip) with a couple of examples.

This is blocking our internal performance sign-off for the POC. Can your team advise on possible mitigations we can apply on our side or if you can temporarily route us to a different capacity tier?

Thanks — Nina
Nina Park
Head of Integrations, Brightlane

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick heads-up — intermittent streaming timeouts in POC

Thanks for the traces, Nina — received and digging in. I'm looping in Rishi and the field/runtime folks to prioritize. High level:

- Short-term ask: we want to try a mitigation tomorrow (4/11) that reduces concurrency pressure for Brightlane routes and toggles one runtime cache knob so your integration can continue while we root cause.
- Long-term: we need a post-mortem outlining the kernel fallback conditions and any model/sequence-length interactions.

Attached: MAP_Brightlane_v2.pdf (updated mutual action plan with a proposed mitigation window and sign-off step). Please confirm the 4/11 16:00 PT window for a controlled change.

Action items for internal team (cc'd):
- Rishi: lead coordination with Brightlane, confirm window and acceptance criteria.
- Karthik & Dev: triage traces, recommend temporary route-level config and rollback plan.
- Hannah: propose telemetry checks and rollback triggers for the change.

Nina — can you confirm the 4/11 16:00 PT slot or propose an alternative?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick heads-up — intermittent streaming timeouts in POC

Poked through the traces briefly. Notes:

- We see repeated kernel-selection fallbacks right before the client-observed timeout window. It looks like the runtime is switching to a slower fallback path under certain sequence-length distributions when concurrency spikes.
- Hypothesis: continuous batching + KV-cache interaction is causing increased tail latency for long-lived streams under high concurrency.

Immediate mitigation I propose (can be toggled per-route):
1) Temporarily set route.max_concurrent_streams = 24 for Brightlane so we don't cross the triggering point.
2) Disable prefix KV cache for Brightlane route (route.kv_prefix_cache = false) — this reduces cache contention at the cost of some token cost.
3) Canary changes to 5% of traffic for 15 minutes -> 25% for 30 minutes -> full move if stable. Have a 10-minute rollback hold if error rate or p95 latency increases >25% vs baseline.

I also want Dev to check whether any quantization/kernel mismatch logs align with the time windows in the traces. If we can reproduce locally, we should build a small repro and fast patch.

Karthik
Principal Field Engineer

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick heads-up — intermittent streaming timeouts in POC

Thanks — I pulled the traces and ran a targeted local replay. Quick findings:

- We do observe kernel fallback events in the runtime log at approximately the same timestamps Nina included. The fallback is triggered when batch shapes vary faster than the kernel cache TTL in the current kernel selector.
- There are no OOMs, but we do see CPU-side stalls while the runtime rebuilds kernel dispatch tables under heavy concurrent inflight sequences.

Short-term patch I can push (non-invasive):
- Decrease default batch_target_tokens from 1024 -> 768 for the Brightlane model route.
- Add route override: "route.runtime_flags.disable_prefix_cache=true" for the Brightlane route.

I've prepared a small diff (SRE_runbook_patch.diff) that contains the change and an automated rollback script. I can kick the canary at the 4/11 16:00 PT window. I'll monitor kernel-fallback counts and p95/p99 latency.

Dev
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick heads-up — intermittent streaming timeouts in POC

Plan for the controlled mitigation (4/11) — operational checklist:

1) Pre-change (T-60m): snapshot route config, capture baseline telemetry (p50/p95/p99 latencies, kernel-fallback-rate, error-rate).
2) Canary rollout (T0): apply route.runtime_flags.disable_prefix_cache=true and batch_target_tokens=768 to 5% of Brightlane traffic. Monitor 1m and 5m windows.
3) Scale canary (T+15m): if stable, 25% for 30 minutes.
4) Full apply (T+45m): move to 100% and keep elevated monitoring for 2 hours.
5) Rollback criteria: any of these triggers -> immediate rollback and paging to on-call runtime: p95 > baseline * 1.25 OR error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute OR kernel-fallback-rate increases by >15% from baseline.

Telemetry hooks: Grafana dashboard INF-POC-Brightlane, Sentry trace filter brightlane_poc.*, and an automated Healthcheck Slack alert to #runtime-ops. I've added the dashboard panels and the alert rule (INF-908).

If Marissa confirms customer availability, we should execute at 4/11 16:00 PT. Dev — please stand by to run the diff and monitor. Rishi/Marissa — please communicate CAB sign-off to the customer.

Hannah
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
